title: The hook: options for the open answers
eyebrow: Area 1 · options only · nothing decided for you

short.lead: Your answers on the comparison page left three things open: a loop line that says what you do, a first spell that is fun without making raids easy, and a few details of the first raid. This page only offers options. Each question has my suggestion marked and room for your own answer.
short.hint: Tap a card to see what it covers. The questions are under Choices.
items: check
Settled
What you already decided
done
The castle hears ordinary talk by default, with an off switch.
Losses show in the world during a raid; numbers appear only in the Lair and Market.
A dead wizard becomes a ghost that whispers, and the castle hears it.
A playtest gate comes after the first build phase.

The first raid starts in the Lair, goes to a pre-chosen Age you can override, carries a visible Ophan demand due at its end, and the Ophan hunts in the last 60 seconds. The demand is easy to find and always obtainable in that Age.
Nothing from you.
bulb
Loop line
A line that says what you do
you
Your rule: it must tell the loop the way 'fish fish, shoot fish, sell fish' does.
The loop today: go into a castle, grab loot, cast spells by speaking, get out before the portal closes, sell in the Market.
Four lines are offered in question 1.
Pick one or write your own.
flask
First spell
A first spell that is fun, not easy
you
Your rule: fun, does not make raids easy, does not hurt progression.
I read 'progression' as: the spell is not one the Market sells, and it does not counter a threat you are meant to buy an answer to.
The options use spells that already work in the game, plus one new idea, because a built spell can be playtested this week.
Pick one or write your own.
list

you

Answer questions 3 to 5.

choices: line
Which line tells the loop?
A
"Steal gold, shout spells, sell gold."
Three verbs, the same shape as How to Fish's line, and the voice is in the middle.
B
"Loot the castle, shout the spells, sell the loot."
Names the place, a little longer.
C
"Grab gold, shout spells, pay the Ophan."
Brings in the master you serve instead of the Market.
D
"Shout spells, steal gold, run."
Leads with the twist and ends on the fear.
It reads in one breath and every word is something you do in the game.
spell
Which spell can a new save use first?
A
Frango, shatter
Breaks locks, doors and walls, and also every fragile thing you are holding. Fun, loud, and it can cost you your haul.
B
Aurum Voco, call the gold
Shows gold through walls for 4 seconds, but you shine too and every guard can see you. Helps find the first demand.
C
Levo, lift
Lift and throw anything, guards included. The most physics comedy, but it makes heavy loot easier, which cuts against your worth rule.
D
A new spell: Vox, throw your voice
Your shout comes from where you point, so the castle that listens hears you somewhere else. Fits the hook, but it is new work and untested.
Frango is already built, makes good clips, and carries its own cost: a careless cast smashes your own loot, so it never makes a raid easy.
length
Is 5 minutes the limit for every raid?
A
Yes, every raid is 5 minutes at most
As you wrote it. The 15 to 25 hour campaign estimate assumed 12 to 15 minute raids, so it gets redone in the campaign area.
B
Only the first raid; later raids run longer
The first raid teaches; later raids leave room for greed.
It is the literal reading of your answer; the campaign length can be fitted to it later.
age
Which Age is the default first raid?
A
High Medieval
The Wick, the one true form already built, lives there, and the Ophan's art exists.
B
Bronze
The earliest Age, so the story runs forward in time.
C
A random Age each new save
Variety, but the opening is harder to tune.
It lets the first raid show a true form that already works.
piece
Where does the first demanded piece sit?
A
In the first big room, lit by the Ophan's lapis glow
Hard to miss, but you still walk away from the portal to get it.
B
In sight of the portal
Impossible to miss, nearly no risk.
C
Anywhere, with its sketch in the ledger
As later demands work; easy to miss on a first raid.
It keeps your 'easy to find, hard to miss' rule while the trip back still matters.
